doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar exists for this contract (checked results/qdrant/v1.18.0/ and whole plugin tree), WebFetch was blocked at network level (domain_blocked condition), fallback web reader fetched the page successfully with canonical URL https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/points/clear-payload. Version: page carries v1.18.x version selector and URL segment v-1-18-x, matches target 1.18.0 major.minor. Content: page states 'Removes the entire payload for specified points.' and request body is PointIdsList OR FilterSelector (exactly the filter-branch the script used); the page says NOTHING about vectors being affected or preserved, so the script's 'vectors unchanged' oracle goes beyond any documented behavior. Endpoint precision: endpoint_registry carries payload+clear POST /collections/{collection_name}/points/payload/clear with doc_quote 'Removes all payload keys of the targeted points; 200 ok / 404.', matching the doc page path and the URL the script registered verbatim in rt.PATHS.

secondary_observations: [A baseline scroll] status=200 raw={"result":{"points":[{"id":0,"payload":{"grp":"a","n":0},"vector":[0.2581989,0.2581989,0.5163978,0.77459663]},... [B readback scroll] status=200 raw={"result":{"points":[{"id":0,"payload":{},"vector":[0.2581989,0.2581989,0.5163978,0.77459663]},... (log line 7, POST-clear: vector byte-identical to line-5 baseline; payload {} = correctly cleared — the raw evidence contradicts the 'vector changed' reading)
[B count count] status=200 raw={"result":{"count":8},"status":"ok"... (log lines 8/13/17: count stayed 8 through all clears — no count drift)
[D] OK: all payloads restored to original (log line 10) and [F] OK: no-match clear returned 200 and mutated nothing (log line 18)

absence evidence: judge_selective ran under-clear/over-clear checks for B (expect_empty=[0-3], expect_intact=[4-7]) and E (expect_empty=[6,7], expect_intact=[0-5]); ZERO UNDER-CLEAR/OVER-CLEAR DEFECT lines were emitted — the payload-key selectivity was exactly correct on both filter branches

comparative (sibling script, same endpoint face rest): output_state_payload_clear_001.log:17 DEFECT: (F) point 1 vector changed after payload clear: [0.2581989, 0.2581989, 0.5163978, 0.77459663] != [1.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0] — clear is payload-scoped — Type4_StateLogicViolation (sibling prints the exact values: got == [1,1,2,3]/sqrt(15), i.e. Cosine normalization of the uploaded original, not a mutation by clear)

comparative (oracle-presence): the only 4 payload_clear scripts carrying the vec_ok-vs-unnormalized-originals oracle are state_payload_clear_001/002/003/004 — all 4 returned DEFECT_FOUND; the 7 sibling payload_clear scripts without that oracle (state_payload_clear_005, boundary_payload_clear_001-006) all returned NO_DEFECT — the verdict tracks the oracle's presence, not endpoint behavior

http_semantics.note: No request-side-decidable error is involved: all three filter-branch clears (grp=a, n>=6, grp=zzz) were valid requests and returned HTTP 200 with the documented envelope {result:{operation_id,status:'completed'}} as expected; the DEFECT verdict rests entirely on a readback comparison, not on error-code semantics.

execution_evidence.reproducibility: stable multi-script trigger (same endpoint payload+clear, same 'vector changed' DEFECT pattern in state_payload_clear_001/002/003/004; all 4 share the identical oracle construction rt.setup_default(C,4,'Cosine') + vec_ok vs un-normalized upload originals; sibling scripts without the oracle all NO_DEFECT)

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys
contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check, horn 1 (wrong-constraint citation): the DEFECT lines allege a VECTOR change, and the observed parameter (vector) lies OUTSIDE the quoted assertion's constraint domain — the assertion governs payload keys only ('after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys') and no constraint in this contract governs vector immutability across payload operations. Horn 2 (genuine compliance) also holds: per the log, the payload-keys assertion was SATISFIED — B readback showed grp=a points with payload {} and zero under-clear/over-clear DEFECT lines, E cleared exactly ids 6-7, count stayed 8. api_violates_assertion=false on both readings. Note also: candidates.jsonl carried constraint_id="" (extractor gap); the id was recovered from the script header 'constraint_ids: qdrant_state_payload_clear_001' and verified present in structured_contract.json constraints.state_constraints.

chain_links: contract: qdrant_state_payload_clear_001 exists in structured_contract.json (constraints.state_constraints); assertion 'after clear, targeted points carry no payload keys' covers payload keys ONLY — it does not mention vectors; candidates.jsonl constraint_id field was empty (mechanical extraction gap), recovered from script header

doc: https://api.qdrant.tech/v-1-18-x/api-reference/points/clear-payload reachable via fallback reader; 'Removes the entire payload for specified points.'; targeting = PointIdsList OR FilterSelector; nothing in the doc attributes any vector effect to this operation — the script's vec_ok 'vectors unchanged' oracle has no doc grounding (it is the script docstring's own inference: 'vectors unchanged after every clear')

script: state_payload_clear_004.py sends the documented filter-branch clears (B {must:[{key:grp,match:{value:a}}]}, E {must:[{key:n,range:{gte:6}}]}, F grp=zzz) to the registry-verbatim URL; BUT it creates the collection with rt.setup_default(C,4,'Cosine') (runtime qdrant.py: PUT /collections/{name} {"vectors":{"size":dim,"distance":"Cosine"}}) and compares scroll readback vectors against the UN-normalized upload originals VECTORS={i:[i+1.0,1.0,2.0,3.0]} with tol=1e-6 (vec_ok, script lines 114/169-174/277-279)

log: VERDICT: DEFECT_FOUND (exit code 1) rests solely on the 16 'vector changed' lines; the log's own raw scroll lines contradict the verdict — line 5 (pre-clear baseline) already shows the normalized vector [0.2581989,0.2581989,0.5163978,0.77459663] and line 7 (post-clear) is byte-identical, so no change occurred across the clear; the mismatch originates at the UPSERT face (ingestion normalization), not the clear face
chain_trace.break_detail: The script judged DEFECT_FOUND but the raw responses recorded in the same log show no vector change: baseline (line 5) and post-clear readback (line 7) vectors are identical, and the 'mismatch' the oracle detected is present in the pre-clear baseline itself (readback = upload/sqrt(15), Cosine normalization at ingestion). The DEFECT verdict is an expected-value artifact of the script's oracle (comparing normalized readback against un-normalized originals in a distance=Cosine collection), not an observed state mutation by payload+clear. Secondary weakness (not the break itself): the vector-stability expectation the verdict enforces is grounded in neither the contract assertion (payload keys only) nor the doc page (no vector statements).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Ingestion path: upsert_point (entry.rs:653) -> NamedVectorStruct::preprocess (named_vectors.rs:296) -> preprocess_dense_vector (:335) -> Distance::preprocess_vector (types.rs:329) -> Distance::Cosine => CosineMetric::preprocess (simple.rs:178) -> cosine_preprocess (simple.rs:228) divides every element by the vector's L2 norm, so under distance=Cosine the STORED (and thus scroll-read-back) vector is the normalized upload. This exactly reproduces the observed numbers: upload [1,1,2,3] -> readback [0.2581989,0.2581989,0.5163978,0.77459663] = [1,1,2,3]/sqrt(15). Clear path: clear_payload (entry.rs:808) -> payload_index.clear_payload(internal_id) + version_tracker.set_payload only; the vector storage is never accessed anywhere in the clear path, so payload+clear structurally cannot mutate vectors.

excluded: env (service healthy throughout: every request 200, zero liveness probes triggered, no 5xx anywhere in the log)
concurrency (script is strictly sequential with 0.5s post-clear sleeps; count stable at 8 across B/E/F; D restore and F no-mutation checks both clean)
cache_delay (readback performed after wait=true + sleep; values identical pre/post, no transient state involved)
mundane_explanation.surviving: script-oracle expected-value flaw: the collection is created with distance=Cosine and Qdrant normalizes vectors at ingestion (simple.rs cosine_preprocess, explicit by-design doc comment), so scroll readback can never equal the un-normalized upload originals the script compares against (vec_ok tol=1e-6). The mismatch is present in the PRE-clear baseline (log line 5) and identical after the clear (line 7) — this fully explains all 16 'vector changed' DEFECT lines without any real state mutation by payload+clear. It is a defect of the test oracle, not of the endpoint.
